newsitem.title: SPAIN: GOLF-RYDER CUP CAPTAINCY A NIGHTMARE, BALLESTEROS SAYS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-RYDER CUP CAPTAINCY A NIGHTMARE, BALLESTEROS SAYS.

text.p: Europe's Ryder Cup captain Seve Ballesteros says the job is "becoming a nightmare".
Eleven months before the match is staged in his home country for the first time, the Spaniard said: "The only thing I will enjoy is when the Ryder Cup starts next year.

"There are so many interviews, so many things to do that it's becoming a nightmare," he told BBC Radio. "I think it's good for the game and good to talk about the Ryder Cup but for the captain it's a little bit too much."

Ballesteros, competing in this week's Masters on the Valderrama course where the Europeans will defend their title against the Americans in 1997, said the responsibilities of captaincy were hampering his game.
"It's difficult to play and talk about the Ryder Cup every day -- Ryder Cup here, Ryder Cup there. It's difficult but I guess that's the way it is.
"I'm not supposed to refuse all the interviews but if I say `yes' to everybody I would not be able to play. I would be doing public relations for the Ryder Cup rather than playing."

The Spaniard said he still hoped to be a playing-captain next September, despite his recent poor form. This weekend will almost certainly see him complete his worst season since he turned professional in 1974.
